chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked him about al-Iman and al-Islam. I said to him, 'Is there a difference between al-Islam and al-Iman?' He said, 'Shall I strike an example for you?' I said, 'Present it.' He said, 'The example of al-Iman and al-Islam is like the Ka'bah al-Haram (the Sacred House) from the Haram (the Sanctuary). One can be in the Haram and not be in the Ka'bah, but one cannot be in the Ka'bah until one is in the Haram. And one can be a Muslim and not be a Mu'min, and one cannot be a Mu'min until one is a Muslim.'
He said, I said, 'So does something exit from al-Iman?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'So to what does it convert him?' He said, 'To al-Islam or to al-Kufr.'

And he said, 'If a man were to enter the Ka'bah and his urine escaped from him, he would be exited from the Ka'bah and would not be exited from the Haram. So he would wash his garment and purify himself, then he would not be prevented from entering the Ka'bah. And if a man were to enter the Ka'bah and urinate therein intentionally (stubbornly), he would be exited from the Ka'bah and from the Haram, and his neck would be struck off.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Islam and Iman according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the hierarchical relationship between Islam and Iman, positing Islam as the necessary foundation for Iman, much like the Haram is the prerequisite for the Ka'bah. It distinguishes between minor impurities that do not break the state of faith and major transgressions that can lead to a complete loss of Iman, potentially reverting one to mere Islam or full Kufr. This analogy underscores the Shia scholarly view that while outward submission (Islam) is essential, true faith (Iman) requires deeper internal conviction and purity.
